newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices fall on low mill demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices fall on low mill demand.

text.p: Indian cotton prices fell on Wednesday on low mill demand and surplus stocks, dealers said.

They said state firms were unloading stocks ahead of the new crop season. In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan fell by 100/400 rupees to 13,200/13,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton eased by 200 rupees to 11,500 rupees.
Bengal-deshi ready delivery fell by five to 840/860 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while October delivery fell by 20/10 rupees to 870/890 rupees. Closing sentiment was subdued.
Indian cotton markets are closed on Thursday for a local Hindu festival. Trading resumes on Friday.
